title: Who was paid from the State homelessness grants
question: Which contractors did San Francisco name to the State as the recipients of its homelessness grant money, and how much has been spent?
finding: San Francisco reported $187.8 million of State homelessness grant money committed across rounds 1 to 5 as of 12/31/2025, $130.0 million of it spent. Two contractors account for 59%: Five Keys Schools And Programs ($75.9 million) and Urban Alchemy ($34.2 million). 1 contractor(s) with $1 million or more committed show nothing spent yet: Glide Foundation ($9.6 million, rounds 4, 5). 14 of the 28 named contractors carry warning signs elsewhere in this project. The State's fiscal snapshot shows the awards for rounds 1 100% spent, 2 100% spent, 3 100% spent, 4 82% spent, 5 39% spent, 6 0% spent.
how: Each grantee must list every funded activity in the State's annual report: who is paid, how much is committed ("obligated") and how much spent. San Francisco files three lists, as a city, a county and a homelessness planning area; all three were added by payee. The totals by round equal the State's award figures. City payments and warning signs are matched to the payee by name.
limits: This money is not on top of what the City pays these contractors; it is one of the sources behind those payments, so it must not be added to the City figure. A large share for two operators reflects who the City chose to run the sites this grant pays for; how they were chosen is a matter for the contract screens, not this one. Nothing spent on a recent round may only mean the work has not started. The payee name is whatever the City typed; a few activities name a City department that then pays others.
